subject: maths
title: Primary 1 Time: Telling Time, am and pm
seo_title: P1 Time Worksheets: Free Primary 1 Maths on Telling Time, am and pm with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Telling time to 5 minutes; use of am and pm; use of h and min; duration of one hour/half hour
meta_desc: Free P1 maths practice on time: o’clock, half past, telling time to 5 minutes, am and pm, and 1 hour or half an hour later. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The short hand shows the hour. Count the long hand in 5s for the minutes.
key_sub: Short hand between 3 and 4, long hand on 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, so it is 3.25.

faq.q: What do P1 students learn about time?
faq.a: In Primary 1, students tell the time to 5 minutes, use am and pm, write hours as h and minutes as min, and find the time 1 hour or half an hour later.

faq.q: How do I teach my child to tell the time to 5 minutes?
faq.a: Read the short hand first for the hour it has passed, then count the long hand in 5s. If the long hand points to 5, it is 25 minutes past, so 3.25.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when reading a clock?
faq.a: Swapping the two hands, for example reading 3.25 as 5.15. Remind your child that the short hand always shows the hour.

faq.q: Is telling time in the P1 MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus teaches telling time to 5 minutes, am and pm, and durations of one hour and half an hour in Primary 1.

items.e: The long hand points to 12. The short hand points to 3. It is 3 o’clock. (12 o’clock reads the long hand as the hour.)
The long hand points to 12. The short hand points to 8. It is 8 o’clock. (12 o’clock reads the long hand as the hour.)
When the long hand points to 12, it is o’clock. The short hand shows the hour: 5 o’clock.
The long hand points to 12. The short hand points to 10. It is 10 o’clock. (12 o’clock reads the long hand as the hour.)
At any o’clock time, the long hand points to 12. The short hand points to 9.
The long hand points to 6, so it is half past. The short hand is between 4 and 5. It has passed 4, so it is half past 4. (Not half past 5: the short hand has not reached 5 yet.)
Half past means the long hand has gone half way around. It points to 6.

At half past 8, the short hand has moved half way from 8 to 9. It is between 8 and 9.
Half past 2 is 30 minutes after 2 o’clock. We write 2.30. (Not 2.50: half an hour is 30 min. Not 2.06: the 6 on the clock means 30 min.)

The long hand points to 6, so it is half past. The short hand is between 10 and 11. It has passed 10, so it is half past 10. (Not half past 11: the short hand has not reached 11 yet.)
Clock B: the long hand points to 12 and the short hand points to 5. Clock A has the hands swapped: its short hand is near 12. C is 6 o’clock. D is half past 5.
Clock C: the long hand points to 6 and the short hand is between 10 and 11. A is half past 9. B is 10 o’clock. D is half past 11.
The short hand moves on from 4 to the next number, 5. So the next o’clock is 5 o’clock. (3 o’clock is before 4 o’clock.)
The clock shows half past 3. Just before it, the time was 3 o’clock. (4 o’clock comes after half past 3.)
The long hand points to 6, so it is half past. The short hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is 11. It is 11.30. (12.30 reads the next number. 6.55 swaps the hands.)
7.30 is half past 7. Clock D: the long hand points to 6 and the short hand is between 7 and 8. A is 7 o’clock. B is half past 1. C is half past 6.
The short hand is between 9 and 10. It has passed 9 but not 10, so it is half past 9. Ali read the next number.
Count in 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes past. (Not 4: count in 5s, not 1s.)
Count in 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 minutes past. (Not 7: count in 5s, not 1s.)
Count in 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. So it is 50 minutes past. (Not 10: count in 5s, not 1s.)
The short hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is 3. The long hand points to 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 3.25. (Not 5.15: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
The short hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is 7. The long hand points to 2. Count in 5s: 5, 10. It is 7.10. (Not 2.35: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
The short hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is 9. The long hand points to 1. Count in 5s: 5. It is 9.05. (Not 1.45: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
The short hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is 6. The long hand points to 4. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 6.20. (Not 4.30: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)

The short hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is 2. The long hand points to 9. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. It is 2.45. (Not 9.15: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
10.25 means 25 minutes past 10. The long hand points to 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. (5 minutes reads the number 5 as 5 minutes.)

The short hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is 11. The long hand points to 8. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. It is 11.40. (Not 8.00: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
The short hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is 1. The long hand points to 7. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. It is 1.35. (Not 7.10: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)

The short hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is 4. The long hand points to 11. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55. It is 4.55. (Not 11.25: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)
3.25: the short hand is between 3 and 4, and the long hand points to 5 (5 jumps of 5 = 25). That is clock C. A is 3.05. B is 5.15 (hands swapped). D is 4.25.
8.40: the short hand is between 8 and 9 and the long hand points to 8 (8 jumps of 5 = 40). That is clock D. A is 8.20. B is 4.40. C is 9.40.
The short hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is 8. The long hand points to 3. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. It is 8.15. (Not 3.40: that swaps the hands. The short hand shows the hour.)

The short hand is close to 8, but it has not reached 8 yet. So the hour is still 7. The long hand points to 10: 10 jumps of 5 = 50. It is 7.50.

items.q: The clock shows 6.35. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: 35 minutes: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. That is 7 jumps of 5, so the long hand points to the 7. (Not the 3 or the 5: those are the digits of 35.)
The short hand is just past 12, so the hour is 12. The long hand points to 2: 5, 10. It is 12.10. (2.00 swaps the hands. 12.02 reads the 2 as 2 minutes.)
The short hand is between 9 and 10, and the long hand points to 7: 7 jumps of 5 = 35. The right time is 9.35. Kavya read the long hand as the hour, so she swapped the hands.

items.q: Times from 12 midnight to 12 noon are ___ times.
items.e: From 12 midnight to 12 noon is the morning part of the day. These are am times. (h and min are for how long something takes.)

items.q: Times from 12 noon to 12 midnight are ___ times.
items.e: After 12 noon it is pm: the afternoon, the evening and the night.
The clock shows 7.30. School starts in the morning, so it is 7.30 am. (7.30 pm is in the evening.)
The clock shows 7 o’clock. Dinner is in the evening, so it is 7 pm. (7 am is in the morning, at breakfast time.)

items.q: Mrs Lim jogs at East Coast Park at this time. When does she jog?
items.e: am times are from 12 midnight to 12 noon. 6.30 am is early in the morning.

items.q: School ends at this time. When does school end?
items.e: pm times come after 12 noon. 1.30 pm is in the afternoon. (Do not mix up am and pm: pm is not the morning.)

items.q: Jun Jie’s family eats dinner at a hawker centre at this time. When do they eat?
items.e: 7 pm is after 12 noon and after the afternoon. It is the evening.

items.q: Raju is fast asleep at this time. When is it?
items.e: 11 pm is late, just before 12 midnight. It is night.

items.q: Which do you most likely do at 7 am?
items.e: 7 am is in the morning, before 12 noon. In the morning you eat breakfast. (Dinner and bed are pm.)

items.q: Which do you most likely do at 9 pm?
items.e: 9 pm is late in the evening. At that time you go to bed. (Breakfast, school and recess are in the morning, so they are am.)
Recess is in the morning, before 12 noon. So it is 10 am. (10 h would mean 10 hours long.)

items.q: Which time is in the afternoon?
items.e: Afternoon times come after 12 noon, so they are pm. 3 pm is in the afternoon. 3 am, 8 am and 11 am are all before 12 noon.

items.q: Which time is in the morning?
items.e: Morning times are am times. 8.30 am is in the morning. The other times are pm.
The clock shows 6.15. He wakes up in the morning, so it is 6.15 am.
The clock shows 8.30. Bedtime is at night, so it is 8.30 pm. (6.40 pm swaps the hands.)
The clock shows 12.30. Lunch is just after 12 noon, so it is 12.30 pm. (12.30 am is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: It is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day. What do we call this time?
items.e: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day is 12 noon. After 12 noon, times are pm. (12 midnight is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Which is the earliest time in the day?
items.e: am times come before pm times. Of the am times, 6 am comes before 11 am. So 6 am is the earliest. (6 pm is in the evening.)

c: They are at the same time.
items.e: Both are pm times. 7 pm comes after 12.30 pm, so dinner is later. (The number 12 is bigger than 7, but 12.30 pm is just after 12 noon.)

items.q: The red arrow shows a time on the day line. Which time can it be?
items.e: The arrow is after 12 noon, in the pm part, in the afternoon. So it can be 4 pm. (4 am is in the am part, before 12 noon.)

sets.title: 1 hour later and half an hour later

items.e: Once around the clock is 60 minutes. 60 min = 1 h. (12 min counts the numbers, not the minutes.)
Half way around is from 12 to 6. That is 30 min, which is half an hour. (6 min reads the number 6. 50 min thinks half of 100.)
In 1 hour, the long hand goes once around: 60 minutes. So 1 h = 60 min. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
1 hour is 60 min. Half of 60 is 30. (Not 50: 1 hour is 60 min, not 100.)
h is short for hour. min is short for minute.
min is short for minute. 30 min is half an hour.

items.q: Ali sleeps for 10 ___ every night.
items.e: Sleep at night is long, so we use hours: 10 h. 10 min is far too short. (am and pm tell the time of day, not how long.)

items.q: Siti brushes her teeth for 2 ___.
items.e: Brushing teeth is short, so we use minutes: 2 min. 2 h would be far too long.

items.q: Which is longer: 1 h or 30 min?
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min is longer than 30 min, so 1 h is longer. (30 is a bigger number than 1, but the units are different.)
1 hour is 60 min. The long hand goes once around and comes back to the same place. The hour goes up by 1: 4 o’clock + 1 h = 5 o’clock.
Half an hour is 30 min. The long hand goes half way around. 2.30 + 30 min = 3 o’clock.
From 3 o’clock to 4 o’clock, the long hand goes once around. That is 1 h. (4 h just reads the end clock.)
From 8.30 to 9 o’clock, the long hand goes from 6 to 12: half way around. That is 30 min.
1 hour is 60 min. The long hand goes once around and comes back to the same place. The hour goes up by 1: 7.15 + 1 h = 8.15.
Half an hour is 30 min. The long hand goes half way around. 10 o’clock + 30 min = 10.30.
1 hour is 60 min. The long hand goes once around and comes back to the same place. The hour goes down by 1: 5.30 − 1 h = 4.30.
The long hand goes from 3 to 9, half way around. 10.15 to 10.45 is 30 min. (45 min reads the end time.)
Half an hour is 30 min. The long hand goes half way around. Count on 20 min to 10 o’clock. Then 10 min more makes 10.10.
Half an hour is 30 min. The long hand goes half way around. 11.45 − 30 min = 11.15.
The long hand is at 8 on both clocks, so it went once around. The hour went from 5 to 6. That is 1 h. (40 min reads the minutes.)
The clock shows 10 am. Count on half an hour (30 min): 10 am → 10.30 am. It is still before 12 noon, so it is am.
The clock shows 4 pm. Count on 1 h: 4 pm → 5 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.
The clock shows 7 pm. Count on 1 h: 7 pm → 8 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.
The clock shows 7.20 am. 7.20 comes before 7.30, so Wei Ming is early, by 10 min.
From 8 pm to 8.30 pm, the long hand goes from 12 to 6. That is 30 min, half an hour. (30 h would be more than a whole day.)
The clock shows 6.45 am. Count on half an hour (30 min): 6.45 am → 7.15 am. It is still before 12 noon, so it is am.
The clock shows 2.15 pm. Count on 1 h: 2.15 pm → 3.15 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.

c: They wake up at the same time.
items.e: Raju wakes up at 6.15 am. Priya wakes up at 6.40 am. 6.15 comes before 6.40, so Raju wakes up earlier.
The short hand is close to 7 but has not reached it, so the hour is 6. The long hand points to 11: 55 min. Dinner is in the evening, so it is 6.55 pm. (7.55 pm reads the next hour.)
Count back half an hour (30 min) from 10 am: 9.30 am. (10.30 am counts on instead of back.)
The long hand is at 6 on both clocks, so it went once around. 4.30 pm to 5.30 pm is 1 h. (5 h reads the hour on the end clock.)
The clock shows 5.20 pm. Count on half an hour (30 min): 5.20 pm → 5.50 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.

items.q: Farah goes to bed at 9 pm. Her little brother goes to bed 1 h earlier. When does he go to bed?
items.e: 1 h earlier than 9 pm: count back 1 hour. 9 pm → 8 pm. (10 pm is 1 h later. 8.30 pm is only half an hour earlier.)
Count back half an hour (30 min) from 3.30 pm: 3 pm. (4 pm counts on instead of back.)
Half an hour + half an hour = 30 min + 30 min = 60 min = 1 h. (30 min counts only one half hour.)
The clock shows 7.15 am. Half an hour is 30 min. 7.15 am + 30 min = 7.45 am. (8.15 am is 1 h later. 7.30 am is only 15 min later.)
The clock shows 11.40 am. Count on half an hour (30 min): 11.40 am → 12.10 pm. After 12 noon the time is pm.
The clock shows 4.10 pm. Count on 1 h: 4.10 pm → 5.10 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.
The clock shows 1.30 pm. Count on 1 h: 1.30 pm → 2.30 pm. It is after 12 noon, so it is pm.
7 am + 30 min = 7.30 am. School starts at 7.30 am, so Devi reaches school just as school starts.
